description: Trigger evaluation for the vendored Anthropic mcp-builder. Positive prompts describe designing, building or evaluating an MCP server; negative prompts describe adjacent work that must NOT pull it in -- consuming an already-running MCP server is not building one, and authoring a skill is skill-creator's job. These prompts were written in this repository to describe the skill's intended trigger surface. They have not been executed as a measurement; attestation.json records the skill as NOT_RUN.

positive_prompts.prompt: I want to expose our internal ticketing API to Claude. Can you build an MCP server for it?
Review my MCP server's tool definitions -- the descriptions and schemas feel wrong.
Write an evaluation suite for the MCP server I just built so I know the tools actually work.
What is the right way to structure tools and error handling in a Python MCP server?

negative_prompts.prompt: Add the GitHub MCP server to my Claude Code config.
negative_prompts.rationale: Configuring an existing server is client setup, not server authoring. Nothing is being built.

negative_prompts.prompt: Create a skill that documents our deployment runbook.
negative_prompts.rationale: Authoring a skill is skill-creator. A skill and an MCP server are different artifacts.

negative_prompts.prompt: Our REST API returns 500s under load. Help me debug the connection pooling.
negative_prompts.rationale: General backend debugging. 'Protocol' and 'server' in the prompt must not be enough on their own.
